bull.b: The executed heads-of-agreement for 7,500 tpa (option to 10,000 tpa) with multi-year term and escalation provisions is a durable commercial milestone. If converted to definitive contracts, it creates predictable long-term volumes that underwrite lender diligence and support project bankability and staged revenue scale-up.

The meta boric acid with materially higher B2O3 (~80% vs 56.3%) and provisional IP filing represents a structural product advantage. Higher purity supports premium pricing and market segmentation (battery, specialty chemicals), boosting potential long-term margins and customer lock-in if qualifications succeed.

A 4x-oversubscribed $36M equity raise materially improves near-term liquidity, extending runway for qualification, commercialization and financing readiness. Combined with a reported low current leverage, this reduces short-term solvency risk and gives management flexibility to pursue EXIM and project finance processes.

bear.b: The company reports no revenue and sustained, material net losses TTM and historically. Without demonstrable, recurring sales, negative margins and operating cash burn persist. This structural lack of revenue requires continued external funding and elevates execution risk until commercial production and contracted sales are realized.

HOAs are important but remain non-binding until definitive contracts linked to finance diligence. Meta boric acid and ferroboron are at trial/qualification stages; delays or failed qualifications would postpone revenue conversion and lender comfort, extending timeline to cash-generating operations and increasing execution risk.

Advancing to FEED and construction depends on external project finance and EXIM diligence that remain incomplete. Historical leverage spikes and ongoing negative free cash flow mean the firm remains dependent on future equity or debt; inability to secure terms would materially delay or scale back the Fort Cady project.
